title: Lookup from the initial search state
statement: Let $k,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $x$ be a finite binary input, let $G$ be a list of groups of transition actions, and let $R$ be a list of remaining actions. Suppose every group has length $3^{k+1}$, the length of $R$ equals the rank read from the input symbol and the symbols under the first $k$ work-tape heads of a configuration $d$, and $d$ is in the recording machine's initial state. Suppose the summary tape, starting two cells beyond its head, marks precisely the group positions: at offset $2+s$ it contains $1$ exactly when $s<|G|$, for $0\le s\le |G|$. Suppose the table tape stores the encoding of the flattened groups followed by $R$, consecutively from its head. Put $A=G\mathbin{\|}R$ and $T=|G|+3+\operatorname{cost}(A)$. Starting the search machine in its observe control state, after $T$ steps it reaches the done control state, with its table and summary heads shifted forward respectively by the encoding length of $A$ and by $|G|+2$. It does not reach the done control state earlier, and through time $T$ its input-head position, tape contents, and output remain unchanged, while every other work-tape head stays fixed. Moreover, $T\le 5$ times the encoding length of $A$, plus $3$.
